title: The Desire Map: A Guide to Creating Goals with Soul
author: Danielle LaPorte
target_audience: Individuals seeking greater clarity and purpose
Those interested in holistic and soulful approaches to goal-setting
People exploring personal transformation and fulfillment
Fans of motivational and spiritual literature
core_themes: Desire as a guiding force for life decisions
Integrating feelings and intuition into goal-setting
primary_purpose: To encourage readers to identify their core desired feelings—how they truly want to feel in life—and to use those feelings as the basis for setting goals, making decisions, and living with greater intentionality and satisfaction.

structure_format.organization: Divided into two main parts: theory (exploring the philosophy and concepts) and practice (step-by-step exercises and worksheets)
features: Worksheets for identifying core desired feelings

key_concepts_lessons: Traditional goal-setting can be disconnected from true fulfillment if it ignores emotional needs.
Core desired feelings are central to making choices that bring meaning and satisfaction.
When you focus on how you want to feel, your goals become more purposeful and authentic.
Clarifying your core emotions leads to better alignment between actions and values.
Self-reflection and soulful inquiry are necessary for lasting transformation.
Achieving goals is less important than feeling good along the journey.
notable_features: Emphasis on feelings as the foundation for personal goal-setting
Journaling and worksheet components for hands-on application
Combination of motivational writing and practical exercises
Strong community engagement through workshops and social sharing
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2012, 'The Desire Map' emerged during a period of growing interest in holistic well-being, mindfulness, and purpose-driven living. It appealed to readers moving away from conventional, productivity-focused self-help toward more introspective, emotion-centered approaches.
reception_impact: Became a bestseller and spawned a movement, with workshops and planner spin-offs
Praised for its fresh perspective on goal-setting and soulful living
Widely embraced by coaching, yoga, and wellness communities
Critics may find the approach too abstract for action-oriented readers
comparable_titles: The Fire Starter Sessions by Danielle LaPorte
The Gifts of Imperfection by Brené Brown
The Universe Has Your Back by Gabrielle Bernstein
